stories.headline: Denver police division chief and her husband, a sergeant, placed on leave after disciplinary investigation
stories.summary:
Denver Police Division Chief Magen Dodge and her husband, Sgt. Justin Dodge, were placed on paid administrative leave Thursday after a disciplinary investigation found they violated department policy, according to the city's Department of Public Safety. Both received letters recommending disciplinary action following a sustained policy violation, spokesman Brent Weisberg confirmed Friday.

The specific allegations have not been released. CBS Colorado, which first reported the leave, previously reported that Magen Dodge was accused of creating a toxic work environment, while Justin Dodge faced allegations of interfering with internal affairs investigations. An independent outside investigator handled the inquiry, and the Office of the Independent Monitor reviewed the draft findings and recommendations.

The couple can present mitigating facts before a final decision is made, and no timeline has been set. Magen Dodge, a 27-year department veteran, won a $280,000 settlement in 2019 over a gender discrimination complaint against former Chief Robert White. Justin Dodge, with 28 years of service, lost part of his left leg when a fire truck struck him during the 2023 Nuggets championship parade and later returned to the SWAT team.

stories.headline: National site selection experts tell Denver business leaders quality of life is not enough to win projects
stories.summary:
Seven national site-selection experts offered candid feedback on metro Denver's competitiveness Thursday at a Denver Metro Chamber of Commerce event at RiNo's ReelWorks, attended by several hundred civic and business leaders. They praised Coloradans' friendliness but said scenery and quality of life do not by themselves attract development.

Kim Moore of the real estate advisory firm Newmark said Denver once ranked in the top 10 for tech, office and financial services projects but has slipped, in part because employers struggled to find talent. She said nonrefundable tax credits mean little to many companies and noted that other states have been willing to change franchise tax laws to land projects, citing a recent one that went to Tennessee. Mike Mullis of J.M. Mullis said Colorado would fit about 20 of every 100 projects he reviews.

Philip Morris International's Darin Early praised the region's cooperation in clearing construction barriers, which allowed the company to open its $1.2 billion ZYN nicotine pouch factory in Aurora near Denver International Airport in July, in half the usual development time.

stories.headline: Great American Beer Festival moves outdoors to Levitt Pavilion for first time
stories.summary:
The Great American Beer Festival opened Saturday at Levitt Pavilion in the Ruby Hill Park neighborhood, its first outdoor edition after more than two decades at the Colorado Convention Center. Thousands of attendees, about 200 breweries and roughly 1,500 beers filled the venue.

Brewers Association president and CEO Bart Watson said organizers wanted to try something new. Changes include pours of up to four ounces and a brewery representative at every booth to pour beers and answer questions about ingredients and brewing. Attendees said the outdoor setting felt more casual, though some noted the heat.

Watson said the move to a different venue reflects the current state of the craft beer industry, where demand has hit a wall while supply kept growing, making the market more competitive. He said the festival also serves as a chance to connect consumers with breweries during a challenging period.

stories.headline: Colorado youth football league barred from state tournament after racial slur controversy
stories.summary:
A season-long controversy over racial slurs and allegations of poor leadership has left 770 young athletes from The Nation Youth Football League barred from the Colorado Football League state tournament, which begins Oct. 31. The CFL terminated its relationship with the Denver-based league, affecting its 28 teams.

The dispute began with a formal grievance from the Park Hill Pirates over an Aug. 15 game against the Denver Mustangs at Pinnacle Athletic Complex in Thornton. Pirates chairman Herman L. White cited racial and derogatory language, postgame hostility and confrontations that escalated to a law-enforcement response. A later incident involving two Mustangs 13U players prompted an emergency CFL meeting, while social media posts inflamed the dispute.

The CFL upheld the ban on Wednesday. Nation Youth Football League president Mikoyan Watson accepted responsibility, attributing the situation to poor leadership and an inability to communicate. The Park Hill Pirates, founded in 1968, have produced NFL players including Calais Campbell and LenDale White.

stories.headline: Historic Barth Hotel in LoDo sells for $2.5 million ahead of $25 million senior housing renovation
stories.summary:
Lakewood-based nonprofit Eaton Senior Communities closed Wednesday on a $2.5 million purchase of the Barth Hotel at 1514 17th St. in downtown Denver, the building's first sale since 1981. The seller was Senior Housing Options, which had operated it as income-restricted senior housing until moving residents out in early 2025 due to deteriorating conditions.

Eaton and developer Sue Powers' Urban Ventures plan a $25 million renovation that will reduce the unit count from 62 to 50 and give each unit its own bathroom for the first time. The building will house low-income seniors. Eaton financed the purchase with a bridge loan from ANB Bank.

The project has funding from the Denver Downtown Development Authority, and U.S. Bank is providing a construction loan and buying historic and low-income housing tax credits. Construction is expected to begin in March, with opening in late 2027 or early 2028. An agreement with hotelier Walter Isenberg required closing by year's end.

stories.headline: Vail home with private observatory listed for $21.5 million
stories.summary:
A Vail home featuring its own commercial-grade observatory has hit the market for $21.5 million. Listing agent Shawn Byrne of Ron Byrne & Associates said the observatory, similar to those on some university campuses, is the defining feature of the three-story, six-bedroom, nine-bathroom house.

The 9,000-square-foot home at 1979 Sunburst Dr. was built in 2010 on 0.6 acres along the Vail Golf Course, with views of the Gore Range. Architect Ned Gwathmey designed it and Colorado-based Shaeffer Hyde Construction built it. The cylindrical observatory sits above an elevator tower, and astronomy themes appear in the interior design and artwork.

Byrne said the property has drawn significant interest and described Vail's luxury market as highly nuanced, with prices varying by location, lot, design and access. Several other homes and estates in the area have sold for between $20 million and $40 million.

stories.headline: One seriously injured, four displaced in Aurora house fire
stories.summary:
One person was taken to a hospital with serious injuries after a house fire in Aurora early Saturday. Firefighters responded to the 20,000 block of East Vassar Avenue at about 12:07 a.m. after multiple 911 calls.

Crews found fire burning in the garage with a vehicle inside, spreading to the home's second level and attic. Eighteen fire and emergency units worked the scene and had the fire under control in about 30 minutes, according to Aurora Fire Rescue spokesperson Samantha Hickerson.

Everyone inside escaped before firefighters arrived. Three people were evaluated at the scene, and the American Red Cross is assisting four displaced residents. The home was heavily damaged, and Aurora Fire Rescue is investigating the cause.

stories.headline: Man killed in shooting on East Ottawa Drive in Aurora
stories.summary:
A man was killed Friday night in a shooting in Aurora, according to the Aurora Police Department. Officers responded just after 9:40 p.m. to the 22000 block of East Ottawa Drive in District 3 for a verbal disturbance that resulted in shots being fired.

Initial investigation indicates two men argued after one was banging on the door of a nearby residence of a woman he knew. The argument escalated, and the shooting occurred in another apartment, police said.

The victim was pronounced dead at the scene and a suspect was detained. The investigation is ongoing, and as of Saturday morning police had not released the identities of the victim or the suspect.

stories.headline: Payton takes back play-calling as 2-2 Broncos visit winless Chargers
stories.summary:
Broncos coach Sean Payton will call plays Sunday at SoFi Stadium, taking the duties back from first-year offensive coordinator Davis Webb after four games. Denver is 2-2 and ranks 28th in total offense at 280.3 yards per game, averaging 18.5 points and just 81.3 rushing yards per game. The team has been outscored 43-13 in the first half and has committed 29 penalties.

Denver faces a Chargers team that is 0-4 and battered by injuries, including offensive tackles Rashawn Slater and Joe Alt and receiver Quentin Johnston. The Broncos are without cornerbacks Pat Surtain II and Riley Moss, with Kris Abrams-Draine and Jahdae Barron expected to fill in. Wide receiver Pat Bryant is also out.

Denver has just eight sacks but 30 quarterback hits and hopes to pressure Justin Herbert. Payton is 2-5 against Chargers coach Jim Harbaugh, and the Broncos are 0-2 on the road this season. Webb will remain coordinator and sit with quarterback Bo Nix between series.

stories.headline: Maple Leafs beat Avalanche 6-3 at Ball Arena behind Nylander's five-point night
stories.summary:
William Nylander scored twice and added three assists as the Toronto Maple Leafs beat the Colorado Avalanche 6-3 at Ball Arena on Saturday. The loss followed a 7-3 Avalanche win over Calgary on Thursday.

Colorado had fallen to 2-1 earlier in the week with a 3-2 loss at Winnipeg, where Kyle Connor broke a tie late with his second goal of the game.

The Avalanche now face a demanding early-season stretch that could show how they measure up.

topStory.headline: Trump Says Ukraine Should Get 'New Leader' After Zelenskyy Criticizes US-Russia Diesel Deal
topStory.summary:
President Donald Trump said Saturday that Ukraine should "get a new leader who can make a deal," a day after announcing an agreement with Russia to suspend sanctions on Russian diesel exports until April 7. Speaking to reporters outside the White House, Trump said Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy "could have made many deals and for some reason, he never does." He also said Zelenskyy "wants to make problems for the world" by authorizing strikes on Russian refineries, adding, "He'd better damn well stop." Trump asserted, without presenting evidence, that Russian President Vladimir Putin strongly wants a settlement and that Zelenskyy is resisting a compromise.

Zelenskyy had criticized the diesel agreement as "terrible" and "not fair and not honest," calling it a "gift" to Putin that would give Moscow revenue to fund its war. The deal was announced while Ukrainian negotiators were in Miami for peace talks, and it appeared to catch Kyiv off guard. Hours later, Russian strikes on south-eastern Ukraine killed 20 people, including three children, with five glide bombs hitting residential buildings in Zaporizhzhia. Zelenskyy said Russia was "expressing its thanks" for the easing of sanctions, and large-scale power outages were reported in Kyiv. The Ukrainian delegation was heading home from Miami on Saturday.

Ukrainian and allied officials responded quickly. Foreign Minister Andriy Sybiga said Zelenskyy has the support of the Ukrainian people, who "have the right to decide," and that statements from abroad "only confirm that he is doing his job well." UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham expressed "complete solidarity" with Zelenskyy in a call, and the two agreed to meet in person in the coming days and to press for an immediate energy ceasefire and an end to attacks on Black Sea shipping. EU foreign policy chief Kaja Kallas said suspending sanctions gives Moscow more revenue for the war, adding, "This is not the time to ease pressure on Russia, and Europe won't," and said European foreign ministers intend to approve the largest sanctions package on Russia since the full-scale invasion.

Russian officials welcomed Trump's remarks. Kirill Dmitriev, Putin's envoy on economic cooperation, called the comments "iconic and historic" and said Ukraine "needs leadership actually focused on peace." A Kremlin aide described Friday's Trump-Putin call as "very substantive and friendly." Russian state media, citing a source, reported that US negotiators Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner may visit Moscow within the next two weeks.

The diesel deal comes amid constrained global fuel supplies, as the US-Israeli war against Iran has effectively closed the Strait of Hormuz, through which roughly a fifth of the world's oil products normally passes. Russia and Ukraine have also intensified strikes on each other's energy infrastructure, further straining markets, and fuel prices are a key issue ahead of November's US midterm elections. Ukraine has been under martial law since Russia's 2022 invasion, which suspends elections. The agreement disrupts four years of Western financial pressure on Moscow and leaves European and NATO allies working to adapt their sanctions strategy, while the planned Witkoff and Kushner trip and the upcoming Burnham-Zelenskyy meeting will indicate how the diplomatic split develops.
